steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Beat in one egg until completely incorporated; beat in last egg along with vanilla extract. Combine flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Stir flour mixture into butter mixture until just incorporated; mix in chocolate chips.
Roll dough into 2-inch balls, or drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart, onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in preheated oven until edges of cookies are firm, 10 to 12 minutes. Remove to wire racks. Dust warm cookies with confectioners' sugar, if desired.

review.reviewBody: My family LOVES this recipe. My girls are dairy free (sadly) so we just sub out the butter for fake stuff and omit the choc chips. DELICIOUS. A big hit at parties too!

Very good, soft chocolate cookie. A basic recipe with lots of room to customize.

Changes: 
-I used 1 stick butter and 1 stick margarine. 
-I used 1.25 cups chocolate chips (to finish the bag)
-I chilled the mixture for 20 minutes (then baked on convection for 12 minutes to make 12 large cookies per batch on a sheet pan)
-I did not sprinkle with powdered sugar

Future Change: when I make these again I will add a pinch of cinnamon so the flavor isn't quite so flat. I would like to experiment with different baking chips i.e. white chocolate, peppermint, peanut butter or butterscotch and/or a combination of nuts and chips.

I like this recipe a lot. I only add a lit bit of milk (1/8 cup) at the end to soften the dough, so it spreads easily while at the oven. I don't mix the chocolate chips, instead I put five or six of them on top of the dough balls. And the most important thing of all: to bake soft cookies you need to use insulated pan sheet, so the cookies don't burn on the bottom. I don't have insulated pan sheet, so I use 2 regular pans, one on top of each other, then I put a parchment paper. I ake them for 10 minutes only, and then I slide the parchment paper into a cooling rack.

I liked this recipe but based on the reviews, made a few adjustments. Seeing that in general the dough falls and leaves a crunch cookie, I added about 1/3 cup of peanut butter (I used crunchy). I also put peanuts in mine instead of chocolate chips. I found it also helped to bake at 340 for the ten mins instead of 350 and please make sure your oven rack is in the very top position so that the source of heat isn't right on the bottoms. I did use the confectioners' sugar. Someone mentioned it wasn't in the directions, but it is. The directions say to sprinkle it on when the cookies were warm. I found it added just the right little extra touch of sweetness. Mine turned out soft and very yummy.

The only changes I made were that I baked at 340 degrees for 9 minutes. They will seem underbaked but once they cool they will be perfect. Oh and I didn't use the chocolate chips. They taste exactly like my favorite packaged cookies from my childhood - Archway Dutch Cocoa cookies. They are soft, chewy, chocolatey and not too sweet. A sugar coating of some kind is definitely necessary! Also, this recipe made about 50-60 cookies! Will definitely make again!

Soft, chocolatey and delicious! These cookies could easily be made into brownies when made right! I baked the first batch on ungreased aluminum foil on a cookie sheet; these came out super chewy and were almost falling apart. If you want that degree of softness, bake them on foil and let them cool for at least ten minutes on the pan before you move them to the wire rack so they don't fall apart.

The second batch I baked on parchment paper, and they were significantly firmer when I moved them to the wire rack. I didn't have to let them cool as long in the pan. Still soft on the inside though!

I'm going to use this as a base recipe in the future for chocolate peanut butter cookies and maybe try to make a copycat recipe for Le Vain/Insomnia Cookies in NYC. Yummy!

These were good but I, of course, made a few tweaks. 1 cup is a boatload of butter/margarine so I used 1/2 cup of margarine and 1/2 of canola oil. I used a stone and a cookie sheet to bake them on. The cookies on the metal cookie sheet came out flat but still ok. The ones on the stone stayed fluffier. With the stone though, I took it out after 10 minutes and they were still doughy. It sat for 10 minutes waiting for the next batch and then I put them in again for 5 minutes. They turned out awesome. I also left out the chocolate chips and these are more than chocolaty enough.

I rarely bake but I can follow recipes. I'm surprised nobody wrote anything about it calling for 2 inch size balls - you'd never get 3 doz cookies that way and they'd come out the size of cake plates. I made them 1/2 inch in size and baked according to the directions. I still had to add at least 3 min baking time because they initially came out raw in the middle. Flavor was good, but too much butter

I make this recipe often for gifts, and it's very popular! I don't add the chocolate chips - with a good quality cocoa, chips are overkill. 

As with any kind of soft-style cookie, the trick is to cook it until the top is just set. It will continue to harden out of the oven, and end up the perfect texture.

i absolutely love these,my boyfriend keeps askong for them.
I bake them for about 8 to 10 minutes and they are perfect.

remember they harden as they cool so take them out super squishy.

Everyone in the family liked this cookie! We chilled the dough for 2 hours before rolling into balls and then rolling in the powdered sugar. In doing this, it yielded 4 dozen instead of three! They seem a little flat, so I might try tweaking some of the ingredients next time to get them to be a puffy cookie, which is what I was looking for this time. The taste is very good. Oh...did not use the chocolate chips.
Imagine the pan edges of a brownie. These cookies are a lot like that, really lovely!

The taste is great, they are soft but, very flat. It's an uneven, bad visual . I make cookies to give away and these make people think they are crunchy by the way they look. I wonder if the butter ratio to flour is too much? One cup of butter is a very big amount for 2 cups of flour
amazing, and quick! perfect for fussy eaters
I did not use chocolate chips, I used 1 cup of Cocoa powder instead. I also substituted the lgiht brown sugar with organic coconut palm sugar. They're delicious and soft. Great recipe
I put Irish Cream liqueur mixed with whipped cream between two. Amazing flavour, big hit with my friends

Good base recipe. Definitely needs some tweaks to make it workable for me. My dough was very moist causing cookies to spread super thin. My next batch I'll be cutting back the butter, adding a little more flour.
My go to cookie for snacks and guests.
